intro.title: Accordion
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple accordion component that allows users to expand and collapse sections of content individually. You will learn how to use Angular's built-in directives, such as *ngFor and *ngIf, to dynamically render and control the visibility of these sections. The core programming concept involves managing component state to track which accordion item is currently open. By the end, you will have a functional, interactive accordion using Angular and TypeScript.
intro.usecase: Accordions are a fundamental UI pattern used to manage content density and improve user experience by allowing sections to expand and collapse. In real software, you'll find them in FAQ pages, where questions are headers that reveal answers, and in settings panels of applications like Slack or Notion, where configuration options are grouped into collapsible categories. As a developer, you'll implement accordions in dashboards to toggle between data visualizations, in forms to reveal advanced options conditionally, and in navigation menus for mobile-responsive designs, ensuring clean, organized interfaces without overwhelming users.
